About SCTL

One platform, so every terminal follows a container the same way.

ConTracker is owned by Sealine Container Terminal Limited (SCTL). It is the container-tracking platform that several bonded terminals share. Each terminal keeps its own jobs, staff, importers and agents. SCTL oversees all of them.

  • Each terminal sees its own work. Staff, importers and agents only ever see the containers of their own terminal.
  • SCTL sees every terminal. Creates and approves terminals, reads cross-terminal reports and sets the platform rules.
  • Customs can look across terminals. Read-only, with Mother Port movements and container search.
ConTracker

What the platform does for a container

Everything that used to travel by phone call, paper and spreadsheet lives on the job itself.

Journey

Live tracking across 15 stages

Each stage has an owner: Field Staff, Operations or Transport. When a stage changes, the importer, the agent and the terminal all see it straight away, and the activity log records who moved it and when.

Documents

Documents stay with the job

Importers and agents upload the Bill of Lading and PAAR. If a document is wrong, staff reject it with a reason, the client sees why, and the corrected file replaces it while the history stays.

Alerts

Compliance alerts

Raised on the job, with the action required.

NAFDACSONNDLEADC RevenueDC ValuationT&TDSS
Returns

Return dates and demurrage

Record the shipping line’s return-by date, the date the container left the terminal and the date it came back. ConTracker counts the days and says whether demurrage was incurred.

Access

Rights per person

Each department has default rights. The terminal Admin can switch any right on or off for one staff member.

Money

Financial reconciliation

Duties collected and outstanding, terminal charges, clearing expenses, invoices and payment status, job by job, visible to Admin and Accountant staff.

Records

Messages and a full activity log

Importers, agents and Customs message the terminal inside ConTracker. Every status change, alert, hand-over and edit is logged with the time, the department and the person.

Why ConTracker

Less chasing. Fewer surprises.

Fewer phone calls

Importers and agents see the stage of their own containers at any time, so nobody has to call the terminal to ask.

Problems show early

Compliance alerts and rejected documents are raised on the job, with the action required and who has to act.

Demurrage under control

Return-by, delivery and return dates sit on the job, and ConTracker counts the days for you.

Everyone sees only theirs

Access is by role and by terminal, and every change is written to the activity log with the person and the time.

The journey

Fifteen stages, three owners

The codes below are the ones staff and clients see on every job. Moving a container along them is a single action, and the order is the order a container really travels.

Field Staff 1 – 9

  1. 01
    CPC-CACCustoms Clearance: Area Controller Approval
  2. 02
    CPC-APMCustoms Clearance: Revenue Verification
  3. 03
    CPC-TSCustoms Clearance: Duty Confirmation
  4. 04
    CPC-ENFCustoms Clearance: Enforcement Review
  5. 05
    CPC-GATECustoms Clearance: Gate Processing
  6. 06
    CPC-FOUCustoms Clearance: Escort Assigned
  7. 07
    MPT-LOADLoading at Mother Port Terminal
  8. 08
    MPT-EXITLeaving Mother Port Terminal (WACT / OMT)
  9. 09
    TRANSITIn Transit to Bonded Terminal

Operations 10 – 13

  1. 10
    BT-ARRArrived at Bonded Terminal
  2. 11
    EXAMUnder Examination
  3. 12
    RELEASECustoms Released
  4. 13
    BT-EXITExiting Bonded Terminal

Transport 14 – 15

  1. 14
    DELIVERYOut for Delivery
  2. 15
    EMPTYReturned Empty

Questions

Common questions

Who owns ConTracker?

ConTracker is owned by Sealine Container Terminal Limited (SCTL), which also oversees the bonded terminals that use it.

What is ConTracker?

A container-tracking platform for bonded terminals, owned by SCTL. It follows a container through 15 stages, from the first Customs approval to the empty container returned to the wharf.

Who can see my containers?

Only people connected to your terminal and with the right for it. Importers and agents see their own containers. SCTL oversees all terminals and Customs officers have read-only access.

Which documents do I upload?

Importers and agents upload the Bill of Lading and PAAR. If staff reject a document, you see the reason and upload a corrected file.

How do I get an account?

Ask your terminal or contact SCTL. A login is created for you and you can change the password yourself.

Is there a mobile app?

Yes. The mobile app and the web app use the same data, so what you see on one matches the other.

How does the demurrage check work?

Enter the shipping line’s return-by date, the date the container left for delivery and the date it came back. ConTracker counts the days and says whether demurrage was incurred.

Can SCTL give me the arrival time of my container?

Yes. Choose your shipping line, send us the container or Bill of Lading number and SCTL will find the estimated time of arrival with the line. ETAs come from the shipping line and can change.

Who do I contact for help?

Call or e-mail Sealine Container Terminal Limited using the details under Contact.
